title: Find the skill search_memory cannot see, and extend it instead of forking a second one
intent: search_memory filters retrieval to {topic, journal, source} (memory.py:434) — it can never return a skill. The skill-manager system prompt nevertheless tells the agent to 'look up the exact id first (search_memory)', advice migration 020 wrote before the type filter mattered. So the obvious move returns nothing, and the obvious conclusion — no such skill exists — is wrong. list_memory is the only granted tool that can see a skill. The corpus makes the wrong turn attractive as well as available: two seeded TOPICS about tool descriptions rank high for this query, so a model that searches gets plausible hits and can end up rewriting a fetched MCP page instead of its own skill.

must_match: (?:when not to|do(?:n'?t| not) (?:use|call|reach)|instead of (?:this|it)|reach for [^.\n]{0,60} instead|is not the (?:right|correct) tool)

source_facts: skills/writing-a-tool-description-other-agents-can-act-on.md already exists and already covers two of the four points the operator listed: say what it DOES not what it IS, and say what comes back.

The two points it does NOT cover are the failure modes (what an `Error:` means for the caller's next step, and what the tool still does not do when it succeeds) and when NOT to reach for it, naming the right tool instead.
search_memory cannot return a skill at all — it filters to {topic, journal, source}. list_memory(kind='skill') returns the id, and read_memory_item on that id returns the full body.

topics/mcp-filesystem-server-tool-descriptions.md is a fetched third-party page listing read_text_file, list_directory and move_file. It is evidence about the problem, not the skill, and it is not this agent's document to rewrite.
topics/nova-builtin-tool-inventory.md is a conversation-tier note counting builtins. Also not a skill.
traps: Searching, finding nothing, and creating a second skill on the same subject. Both then get injected by skills_context and the reader has to pick.
Following the agent's own system prompt, which says to look the id up with search_memory — advice that predates the type filter and cannot work for a skill.

Updating topics/mcp-filesystem-server-tool-descriptions.md because it ranked first and is about tool descriptions. It is a captured web page; editing it destroys a record of what that server actually advertised.
Pasting the MCP server's example descriptions into the skill, which turns operating guidance into a transcript of somebody else's API.
Rewriting the two sections that were already correct, so the diff is unreviewable and the operator cannot tell what actually changed.
judge.guidance: discovery and duplicate_avoidance are the point: the winning run is the one that ends with ONE skill on this subject holding all four points. Either mode is legitimate — append the two missing sections, or replace with a merged document — but a replace must keep the two existing sections intact. Score source_discipline on leaving both seeded topics untouched and on not importing the MCP server's strings as if they were house guidance.
